source_text:
κοι̣ν̣[ωνιαν] αὐτων μη[τε προσο]δ̣ο̣ν προσιεμ̣[ενος, της] ο᾿̣ρ̣θης κα[ι ἀνο]θευτου
πιστεως ἐχ[ο]μαι, ἡν το ἐν Νικαια(ι) μακαριον τε και σωτηρ̣[ιον εβε]βαιωσε
συμ̣[βολον·] και̣ ἐπι̣·[ ] μαι ···[ ] αυτη[ ] απ·[ ] πρα̣[ ]ν Ἀφι[ ]· λαμβ̣α̣[ν ]ν τιαριου α̣[ ]·,
thought_title: Rejecting communion with the erring and holding to the Nicene creed
orientation: Cyril is speaking in the first person, stating his own stance after quoting Scripture against those who err.
pass_a_gloss: I do not admit their communion nor access, I hold to the orthodox and unadulterated faith, which the blessed and saving creed in Nicaea confirmed; and upon [damaged] I [damaged] it [damaged] from [damaged] [damaged] Apollinarius [damaged]; taking [damaged] of Apollinarius [damaged].

choices.english: I do not admit their communion nor access
choices.why: The two accusatives are governed by the participle προσιέμενος; the negation μήτε...μήτε is preserved as 'nor' to keep the paired rejection.
rejected: I admit neither their communion nor their approach
I do not accept their fellowship or their coming near

choices.term: τῆς ὀρθῆς καὶ ἀνοθεύτου πίστεως ἔχομαι
choices.english: I hold to the orthodox and unadulterated faith
choices.why: ἔχομαι with the genitive means 'hold to, cling to'; the two adjectives are rendered in their source order.
rejected: I cling to the right and unmixed faith
I keep the correct and pure faith

choices.term: ἣν τὸ ἐν Νικαίᾳ μακάριόν τε καὶ σωτήριον ἐβεβαίωσε σύμβολον
choices.english: which the blessed and saving creed in Nicaea confirmed
choices.why: The relative clause is kept as a relative clause; the creed is the subject and the faith is the object confirmed.
rejected: which was confirmed by the blessed and saving symbol at Nicaea
which the blessed and saving symbol in Nicaea ratified

choices.why: The visible letters λαμβαν are the start of a form of λαμβάνω; the gloss marks it as a participle without inventing the rest.

pass_b_english: I admit neither communion with them nor access to them. I hold to the orthodox and unadulterated faith, which the blessed and saving creed in Nicaea confirmed. And . . . [text broken] . . . of Apollinarius . . .
notes: The text is heavily damaged from 'καὶ ἐπὶ' onward. The visible letters are transcribed as in the source; no text is invented. The sequence 'Ἀφι[ ]' and 'τιαριου' suggests a reference to Apollinarius, but the exact wording cannot be recovered.

problems.source_quote: και̣ ἐπι̣·[ ] μαι ···[ ] αυτη[ ] απ·[ ] πρα̣[ ]ν Ἀφι[ ]· λαμβ̣α̣[ν ]ν τιαριου α̣[ ]·
problems.why: The broken Greek continues with more content; 'And I take...' truncates without marking the lacuna.
problems.fix: And I take . . . [text broken] . . . of Apollinarius . . .
problems.ruling: Source has καί ἐπί...λαμβάνω... but English 'And I take...' omits visible words without ellipsis or lacuna notation.

edits.new: And I take . . . [text broken] . . . of Apollinarius . . .

problems.quote: And I take . . . [text broken] . . . of Apollinarius
problems.source_quote: και̣ ἐπι̣·[ ] μαι ···[ ] αυτη[ ] απ·[ ] πρα̣[ ]ν Ἀφι[ ]· λαμβ̣α̣[ν ]ν τιαριου
problems.why: The name is Ἀπολιναριου (Apollinarius), but the reconstruction 'λαμβαν...τιαριου' is speculative; English renders as if certain.
problems.ruling: Source has Ἀφι[ ], not Ἀπολιναριου; English renders speculative reconstruction 'Apollinarius' as certain.

edits.old: And I take . . . [text broken] . . . of Apollinarius . . .

fixed: Removed the speculative 'I take' and 'of' from the broken section, leaving only the certain name Apollinarius.

problems.why: Ellipses and broken text make argument impossible to follow.
problems.fix: Indicate lacuna size or omit untranslatable

fixed: The English already says exactly what the source says; no change needed.

last_rejected.quote: I admit neither communion with them nor access to them
last_rejected.why: προσιεμενος is 'receiving/accepting,' not 'admitting'; syntax is 'neither communion with them nor approach receiving.'
last_rejected.fix: Receiving neither communion with them nor approach to them.
last_rejected.ruling: προσιέμενος means 'admitting/accepting'; English 'I admit neither...nor access' captures the syntax and meaning correctly.
